subject: science
title: Sun and Shadows
about: The sun's daily pattern (up in the east, high at midday, down in the west, light and heat) and the shadows it makes: long in the morning and evening, short at midday, always on the side away from the light (ESS.1.1.1). Shadows are not named in the Grade 1 standard; they are the easiest way for a child to see the sun's apparent movement, so this is a bridge inside ESS.1.1.1.
tip: Trace his shadow with chalk after breakfast, at lunch and before dinner, then compare the three.

cards.q: In the morning, which part of the sky does the sun seem to come up in?
cards.note: We say the sun rises in the east.

cards.q: In the evening, which part of the sky does the sun seem to go down in?
cards.note: We say the sun sets in the west.

cards.q: Does the sun seem to come up in the same part of the sky every morning?
cards.note: Up in the east, down in the west, every single day. That is a pattern.

cards.q: A sidewalk has been in the sun all afternoon. How does it feel?
cards.note: The sun gives us heat as well as light.

cards.q: On a hot day, where is it cooler, in the sun or in the shade?
cards.note: Shade is the shadow of a tree or a building. Less of the sun's heat reaches there.
Light cannot go through you, so a dark shape shows on the other side.

cards.q: The sun is in front of you. Where is your shadow?
cards.note: Your body blocks the sunlight, so the dark spot is behind you.

cards.q: Is a shadow on the side toward the light or on the side away from it?
cards.note: Try it with a flashlight and a toy.

cards.q: In the early morning the sun is low. Is your shadow long or short?
cards.note: When the sun is low, shadows stretch out long.

cards.q: At midday the sun is high in the sky. Is your shadow long or short?
cards.note: When the sun is high, your shadow is short and close to your feet.

cards.q: In the evening the sun is low again. What does your shadow do?
cards.note: Long in the morning, short at midday, long again in the evening.

cards.q: Your shadow points a different way in the afternoon than in the morning. What seemed to move?
cards.note: As the sun seems to cross the sky, shadows swing around and change length.

cards.q: There is no sunlight at night. What happens to your sun shadow?
cards.note: No light, no shadow. A lamp or a flashlight can still make one.

cards.q: You walk across a sunny yard. What does your shadow do?
cards.note: Your shadow stays joined to your feet wherever you go.

cards.q: A cloud drifts in front of the sun. What happens to your shadow?
cards.note: Less light means a fainter shadow. When the cloud moves on, it comes back.

cards.q: You want to know where the sun is. What is the safe way to find out?
cards.note: Never look right at the sun. Your shadow points away from it.
